newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy 1996 deficit may reach 137 trln lire - paper.
newsitem.headline: Italy 1996 deficit may reach 137 trln lire - paper.

text.p: Italy's budget deficit may total 137 trillion lire or more in 1996 rather than the 135 trillion expected by the Treasury, daily Il Sole 24 Ore said.

The paper, which gave no source for its report, said the deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) ratio for 1996 was likely to outstrip the 7.3 percent of 1995 although the debt to GDP ratio was still likely to register a slight improvement.
It noted the deficit figures were provisional and said the cause of the overshoot seemed to be regional authorities and public bodies bringing forward requests for funds into 1996 from 1997.
"As soon as public bodies suspected the government intended to put limits on the demands on the accounts, the reaction was immediate," Il Sole said.
Withdrawals by those authorities had intensified at the end of December to get in before the start of January, it said.
The government's target deficit to GDP ratio for this year was 6.6 percent but the ratio is now expected to be around seven percent.
The government's target public sector borrowing for 1996 was 123 trillion lire but November's cumulative PSBR, according to Treasury data, was 135.3 trillion lire.
